feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital/public-sector communications leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target brand. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some structure and style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, studio buildout.  
- Strong positioning for digital platform leadership through a mix of strategy, governance, CMS, analytics, multimedia, and AI/search work.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics—for example, improvements in engagement, efficiency, search performance, publishing speed, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists varies; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found, but wording is occasionally repetitive (“supporting,” “strengthened,” “improve”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground scale/recency: “12+ years leading enterprise digital platforms and communications systems for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct outcomes-oriented language: “driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and editorial operations.”
- Consider adding one concrete differentiator already supported elsewhere, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “50+ publishers,” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Smooth parallel structure: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” and the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” are repetitive.
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies; use the intro for positioning, not another skills inventory.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, more executive phrasing: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight systems.”
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths first; consider grouping around strategy, platforms, analytics, and communications operations.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” for stronger ownership language.
- Consider revised version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it concise and avoid listing tools or lower-level tasks here.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets; retain only if targeting communications-focused roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Standardize verbs and structure: “Built/Developed/Launched…” + what it was + why it mattered.
- Replace vague phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper wording such as “built for reuse and expansion.”
- If possible, add 1–2 concrete outcomes or scale markers; otherwise emphasize unique scope (e.g., “10×20-foot interactive conference display”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo roles; avoid repeating the same wording from Work Experience.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to add variety.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and AI/search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, enterprise web modernization, and content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with sharper consulting language: “Designed and implemented cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate Drupal/CMS bullets: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits; provided front-end/CMS troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”
- End with the strongest differentiator: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, users, teams, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; frame this as advisory/consulting impact rather than ownership.
- Specific projects like the microsite and AI search already appear in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level unless adding measurable results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel and analytics bullets more measurable: add team size, budget size, email list size/open-rate gains, social growth/engagement, reporting speed, or decision-making improvements if available.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “including”/“along with” constructions with direct verbs; e.g., “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as building organizational capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the more senior Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around execution leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Combine overlapping workflow bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”
- Make outputs more concrete: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen video impact: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound tentative; use direct ownership to avoid underselling.
- Avoid repeating broader governance/operations language already covered more strongly in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance & editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for a more senior phrase like “Content operations and planning” or “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Keep terminology aligned with recent experience: “content governance,” “editorial operations,” and “cross-channel” better reflect the 2022–Present work.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web and content strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” closely duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies: “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless central to target roles; WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages dilute the stronger enterprise web narrative.
- If possible, add scope in adjacent experience bullets instead of here (e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “50+ publishers,” “3.5M annual page views”) since skills sections rarely need standalone metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” or “Analytics infrastructure, insight generation & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO and web performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views” rather than listing more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is near-duplicate of Technical + IT → “Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section strategic/capability-focused and leave the detailed tool inventory there.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent in-house studio/event leadership rather than basic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and delivery level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event production”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a stronger, broader phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to signal seniority.
- Consider combining “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” into one outcome-oriented line to reduce fragmentation.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to evidence from recent roles (e.g., built NACo’s first in-house studio; supported advocacy programming and event production).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with leadership-level phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most credible/recent tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it was used meaningfully in recent work.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for impact: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use “CMS & Web Platforms” if you want a cleaner, more standard heading.
- If GitHub Pages stays, place it last and only if it supports a portfolio/side-project angle.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, cleaner terms: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Clarify applied technical scope: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add level/context to avoid sounding entry-level: “for Drupal-based sites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version-specific labels unless important: use “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates Topline Skills [2] almost verbatim (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); either consolidate or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you want this item strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears elsewhere, this item should emphasize systems you actively built or managed and group collaboration tools more tightly.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**
- Consider trimming to 6–8 strongest tools to keep focus on automation systems, not general workplace apps.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less differentiation than Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement leadership. Given the strong recent NACo email work, this item should better signal enterprise-scale communications systems and audience engagement operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parenthetical form: **Higher Logic (enterprise member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (customer journey automation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- If space allows, tie to function rather than just tools: **Newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation, and engagement campaigns**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capability, not just software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **KPI reporting** or **performance reporting** for a sharper business outcome focus.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work instead of more tools, e.g. **supported reporting for a 10,000+ page site with 3.5M annual page views**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the fuller version in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same stack multiple times.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete by emphasizing foundational team-building, platform/content contributions, and any measurable production or workflow impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add specific outputs/results if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, email/social volume, or workflow time saved.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic verbs: “strengthening workflows” → “standardized publishing workflows across web, email, social, and video.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized multi-channel publishing workflows, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “guidance to a digital media associate” may feel minor next to later leadership roles unless framed as early supervisory responsibility.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to foreground scope and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend member-facing communications.”
- Tighten the podcast line: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a more concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for program and policy teams, while supporting digital content and multimedia production. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video or channel leadership here; later positions demonstrate that progression better.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Multimedia Production Tools** for clarity and consistency.
- Separate software from capabilities; e.g. **Adobe Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator**.
- Replace vague phrasing with stronger, industry-standard terms: **livestream studio operations** instead of “livestream studio workflows.”
